key_insight: In solid molecular hydrogen, including multiple particle–hole transitions in QMC changes exciton localization substantially while barely changing excitation energies.
engineering_relevance: Accurate modeling of optical response and excitation-induced forces requires checking exciton localization, not just excitation energies.
method: Model the lowest neutral excitation of phase-I solid hydrogen under compression using QMC.
Compare single-substitution and multideterminant excited-state wave functions.
Benchmark against BSE and TDDFT across nuclear configurations representing thermal and quantum fluctuations.
evidence_signal: At low density, multideterminant QMC matches or exceeds BSE exciton localization, while TDDFT generally predicts more extended excitons; differences diminish under compression.
watch_item: QMC–BSE agreement in transition dipoles and excitation-induced forces can deteriorate for nuclear configurations with substantially different predicted localization.
paper_title: Excitons in solid molecular hydrogen from quantum Monte Carlo
